title: Bulk edit owner, status and dates for several features
subtitle: Mock-ups for the owner to pick from: how features are picked (BE1), the bulk bar (BE2), mixed rights (BE3). Priorities, ranked list, Simple; invented data.

decisions.name: Picking several features
decisions.question: How does a person pick several features on a list without losing drag to reorder or click to open the panel?
decisions.common: Shown on Priorities, ranked list (Simple), at 1440 and 1512 and on a phone. Picked rows get the accent ring; the bulk bar (BE2) shows once one row is picked; Clear and Esc drop the picks. Proposal A is also drawn on the Roadmap Now / Next / Later board and the Detailed plan table. Not drawn: B and C on the board, and any proposal on Goal buckets, Inbox or the Roadmap timeline; each would pick the same way as on Priorities. Today: no picking at all; fixing 4 features means 4 panel opens (about 16 steps).

proposals.name: Boxes on hover
proposals.what: A checkbox fades in left of the drag handle when the pointer is over a row, and stays on every row once one is picked. Shift-click on a second box picks every row between. "Pick all N shown" sits over the list while picking. The handle still drags, the name still opens the feature panel. On a phone the boxes always show.
proposals.why: Nothing changes for someone who never picks, drag and click keep working, and it is the way Jira and Linear lists already work, so people know it.
proposals.plus: Shift-click covers "the 8 overdue ones" in two clicks; works the same with a mouse, a keyboard (Space on the box) and a finger.
proposals.cost: 2 clicks for a run of rows, 1 click per row otherwise; nothing to turn on or off.

frames.caption: At rest: the list looks as it does today. No boxes until the pointer is on a row.
The pointer on Alert rules engine: its box fades in left of the drag handle.
Alert rules engine is picked; with Shift held over Alert history export, the rows between are tinted to show what Shift-click will pick; the list ends above the bar.
After the Shift-click: 5 rows picked, every box shows, "Pick all 22 shown" shows part-picked, the bar says "5 picked". The dashed note in the left menu gives the clicks against today.
The same result in dark mode.
Hard case, 1512 wide, all 22 picked with "Pick all 22 shown", scrolled to the end: the bar stays at the bottom and the last row ends above it.
Phone 390: no hover, so every row shows its box; 3 rows picked by tapping their boxes, the list ends above the bar.
The same phone frame in dark mode.
The same on Roadmap, Now / Next / Later: the pointer on a card shows its box in the top-right corner; the rest of the card still drags and opens the panel.
One card picked; every card now shows its box.
Shift-click on a card further down Now picks the run down the column: 4 picked, the same bar. Cost: 2 clicks.
Board at 1512 wide: a card in Later added with one more click, so picks span columns; the page scrolled to it, so the Next cards sit above, out of view.
Board on a phone 390: boxes always show; 2 cards picked by tapping; the bar sits above the bottom tabs with all its fields.
The same board phone frame in dark mode.

Detailed, scrolled to the plan table: a box column first, as tables do; boxes always show here, the header box picks all shown. The Detailed page has its own example plan, so names differ from Priorities; the item open on the right keeps its own tint.
Detailed: box on row 2, Shift-click on row 6 picks the run across the Now and Next groups; picked rows tint and the same bar shows. A row click still opens the item on the right. Cost: 2 clicks.
Detailed at 1512 wide: two rows picked one by one, the run is not needed.
Detailed on a phone 390: the box sits right of each item's name; 2 picked.

proposals.name: A pick mode
proposals.what: A "Pick several" button over the list turns on a pick mode: drag handles give way to checkboxes and a click anywhere on a row picks it (Shift-click picks a run). "Done picking" turns it off.
proposals.plus: Big click targets, no hidden controls; nobody drags a row by mistake while picking.
proposals.cost: 1 click to start, 1 per row (or 2 for a run), 1 to finish: 4 to 5 clicks for 4 rows.

frames.caption: At rest: a "Pick several" button over the list; rows as today.
Pick mode on: the drag handles become boxes, drag is off (its tip says why), the button reads "Done picking".
Two rows picked by clicking anywhere on them.
Shift-click on row 7 adds the run 4 to 7: 5 picked and the bar shows. The dashed note in the left menu gives the clicks against today.
The same result in dark mode.
Hard case, 1512 wide with long names: the pointer is still on Mobile alert push's name, just clicked; the row got picked and no panel opened, so the panel is two clicks away while picking.
Phone 390: "Done picking" shows the mode is on; rows 2 and 3 picked (row 3 is just below), the handle space holds the box.
The same phone frame in dark mode.

proposals.name: Ctrl and Shift click
proposals.what: No new control: Ctrl-click (Cmd-click on a Mac) on a row picks it, Shift-click picks a run, as in a file manager. A small "Pick several" (i) over the list says how.
proposals.plus: Zero new things on screen; the fastest for people who already know the keys.
proposals.cost: 2 clicks for a run, 1 per row, but only with a keyboard; no way on a phone or tablet.

frames.caption: At rest: only "Pick several" with its (i) over the list.
Ctrl-click on Alert rules engine picks it; the bar shows "1 picked".
A second Ctrl-click adds Mobile alert push.
Shift-click on row 7 adds the run 4 to 7: 5 picked. The dashed note in the left menu gives the clicks against today.
The same result in dark mode.
Hard case, 1512 wide with long names, the pointer on Mobile alert push: nothing on the row says it can be picked; a person who has not read the (i) never finds it.
Phone 390: a tap has no Ctrl or Shift, so nothing can be picked; this proposal needs a second way for touch.
The same phone frame in dark mode.

decisions.name: The bulk bar
decisions.question: Where does a person set owner, status, dates or track for the picked features, and see what will change before it does?
decisions.common: Every proposal: owner (people), status (New, In progress, Exists: the product's own words), end date set to a day or shifted by weeks, track; a before -> after preview; one button that applies all, one history entry per feature, one toast with Undo. 4 features picked (ranks 2, 4, 6, 7) on Priorities. Today: 4 panel opens, about 16 steps.

proposals.name: Bar with field menus
proposals.what: A bar sits at the bottom, with the list ending above it: "4 picked · Clear | Owner Status Dates Track". Each field opens a small menu above the bar; once a value is picked the menu lists every feature before -> after (features that already have it say "already") with Cancel and "Change 3" (it counts only the features that change). Applying closes the bar and shows a toast with Undo.
proposals.why: One field at a time is what people do most ("give these an owner", "mark these done"); the preview sits right by the choice, and nothing covers the list until a field is opened.
proposals.plus: Short: 3 clicks after picking; the preview names each feature, so a wrong pick is seen before applying.
proposals.cost: Pick (2) + field (1) + value (1) + Change (1) = 5 clicks for any number of features (today: about 16 for 4, 32 for 8).

frames.caption: At rest: 4 rows picked, the bar at the bottom with Owner, Status, Dates and Track.
Status opened: a menu above the bar with New, In progress and Exists.
Exists picked: the menu lists the 4 features before -> after, "already Exists" where nothing changes, and "Change 3", the 3 that do.
Dates opened instead: set the end date to a day, or shift it by weeks; Dec 15 picked, the preview lists each end date before -> after.
Track opened: the tracks to move the 4 features to.

"Change 3" pressed with Exists: the 3 that changed show the product's Exists pill with a tick beside it, the Show counts update, the picks clear (Alert routing by team, already Exists, keeps its owner line and gets no tick), a toast says 3 changed with Undo. The dashed note in the left menu gives the clicks against today.
The same result in dark mode.
Hard case, 1512 wide, 14 picked with long names, dates +2 weeks: the preview shows 5 and "and 9 more", the menu scrolls.
Phone 390: the bar takes two rows (count, then the 4 fields); the menu opens full width above it.
The same phone frame in dark mode.

proposals.name: One edit sheet
proposals.what: The bar holds a single "Edit 4 features" button. It opens a side sheet with all four fields (each left as "keep" until set) and a "What changes" list under them; one "Change 4" applies everything set.
proposals.plus: Several fields in one go (owner and dates together) with one preview and one Undo.
proposals.cost: Pick (2) + Edit (1) + 2 per field + Change (1): 6 clicks for one field, 8 for two.

frames.caption: At rest: 4 picked; the bar has one "Edit 4 features" button.
The sheet opened on the right: Owner open, Status, Dates and Track on "keep"; the bar hides while the sheet is open.
Track opened in the sheet: the tracks to move the 4 features to.
Owner Rosa Lind and dates +2 weeks set: "What changes" lists each feature's owner and end date before -> after.
"Change 4" pressed: rows show Rosa Lind and their new end dates, the sheet closes, a toast offers Undo. The dashed note in the left menu gives the clicks against today.
The same result in dark mode.
Hard case, 1512 wide, 14 picked with long names: the preview shows 3 and "and 11 more", which opens the rest; the list stays in view on the left, the bar is hidden.
Phone 390: the sheet covers the whole screen; Owner set to Rosa Lind.
The same phone frame in dark mode.

proposals.name: Preview in the rows
proposals.what: The bar is the same as A, but a field's menu only takes the value and closes; the preview is drawn in each picked row itself (old value struck, new value beside it) and the bar gets "Change 4".
proposals.plus: The change is seen where the feature lives, next to its rank, goal and score.
proposals.cost: Pick (2) + field (1) + value (1) + Change (1) = 5 clicks; checking picks that are off screen needs scrolling.

frames.caption: At rest: 4 picked, the same bar as A.
Dates opened: set the end date to a day, or shift it by -2, -1, +1, +2 or +4 weeks.
Track opened: the tracks to move the 4 features to.
+2 weeks picked: the menu closes and each picked row shows its end date struck and the new one beside it; "Change 4" appears in the bar.
"Change 4" pressed: rows keep the new end date in the edited colour, a toast offers Undo. The dashed note in the left menu gives the clicks against today.
The same result in dark mode.
Hard case, 1512 wide, 14 picked with long names: only the 4 picks on screen can be checked; 10 sit below the fold.
Phone 390: the preview is in each card (Alert rules engine: end Nov 10 struck, Nov 24); with long cards only one or two picks are on screen at a time.
The same phone frame in dark mode.

decisions.name: Mixed rights
decisions.question: When some picked features will become proposals and some cannot be changed at all, how does the person know before and after applying?
decisions.common: Rights come from each feature's own can_* fields: a feature's owner or approver changes it at once, anyone else's change becomes a proposal to that feature's approver, a locked feature is not changed. Shown with the BE2 A bar, signed in as Lena Vos, an approver; 4 picked: two Lena approves, Weekly alert digest F-79 (Avery Stone approves it, so the change goes to Avery Stone) and Alert routing by team (locked by Jonah Pike). Avery Stone also approves Alert history export.

proposals.name: Sorted preview
proposals.what: Picked rows carry a small "Proposal" or "Cannot change" tag. The preview splits into "Changes now", "Sent to Avery Stone to approve" and "Not changed" (with an (i) saying why), and the button says "Change 2, propose 1". After applying, a strip over the list reads "Owner Rosa Lind: 2 changed · 1 sent to Avery Stone · 1 not changed"; each count highlights its rows, with Undo.
proposals.why: Nothing surprises the person: they see the split before pressing and can find every item after, while all four stay pickable.
proposals.plus: One apply for the whole mix; the counts lead to the rows they count.
proposals.cost: The same 5 clicks as BE2 A; 1 more to see which rows were not changed.

frames.caption: At rest, signed in as Lena Vos, an approver: 4 picked, scrolled to Alert routing by team, tagged "Cannot change"; Weekly alert digest above it is tagged "Proposal".
Owner opened: the five people.

Rosa Lind picked: the preview splits into Changes now 2, Sent to Avery Stone 1, Not changed 1 with its reason ("Locked by Jonah Pike for the Dec 15 board meeting"); the button says "Change 2, propose 1".

Applied: Alert routing by team keeps its owner, Jonah Pike, and its "Cannot change" tag, Weekly alert digest reads "Rosa Lind, waiting for Avery Stone", and the strip counts 2 changed, 1 sent, 1 not changed, each a button. The dashed note in the left menu gives the clicks.
The same result in dark mode.

Hard case, 1512 wide, signed in as Mei Arden, a commenter: each change goes to that feature's own approver: the bar says her changes go to each feature's approver (its (i) names Lena Vos and Avery Stone), the preview splits into "Sent to Lena Vos to approve · 2" (Alert rules engine, Mobile alert push) and "Sent to Avery Stone to approve · 2" (Weekly alert digest, Alert history export), and the button says "Propose 4 changes".
Phone 390: the result strip with its three counts, above the list; rows 1 to 3 under it.
The same phone frame in dark mode.

proposals.name: Locked rows not pickable
proposals.what: A feature the person cannot change shows a lock where its box would be (its tip says who locked it and why), so it is never picked. Proposals are picked as usual; the button says "Change 2, propose 1" and the toast says how many went to the approver.
proposals.plus: Nothing is ever "not changed": the result is always all applied or proposed.
proposals.cost: The same 5 clicks; a shift-click run skips locked rows silently.

frames.caption: At rest, signed in as Lena Vos, an approver: 3 picked; Alert routing by team shows a lock instead of a box.
Owner opened: the five people.
Rosa Lind picked: a plain preview of the 3, and "Change 2, propose 1".
Applied: a toast "2 changed, 1 sent to Avery Stone to approve" with Undo; Weekly alert digest reads "Rosa Lind, waiting for Avery Stone". The dashed note in the left menu gives the clicks.
The same result in dark mode.

Hard case, 1512 wide, signed in as Mei Arden, a commenter: every box stays (all can be proposed); each goes to that feature's own approver, so the bar says her changes go to each feature's approver, its (i) naming Lena Vos and Avery Stone; the button says "Propose 4 changes".
Phone 390: the result as a toast at the bottom; rows 1 to 3 above it.
The same phone frame in dark mode.

proposals.name: Apply, then report
proposals.what: No rights are shown before applying: the button says "Change 4". After it, a strip over the list lists what was not changed, each with its reason and an "Ask Jonah Pike" button, and counts the proposals sent.
proposals.plus: The plainest bar; the "why" and the way out sit together after the fact.
proposals.cost: The same 5 clicks, plus 1 per locked feature to ask its owner.

frames.caption: At rest, signed in as Lena Vos, an approver: 4 picked; no tags on the rows.
Owner opened: the five people.
Rosa Lind picked: a plain preview, "Change 4", nothing said about rights.

Applied: the strip over the list counts 2 changed, 1 sent, 1 not changed and lists Alert routing by team (its row keeps Jonah Pike as owner), "Locked by Jonah Pike for the Dec 15 board meeting", with "Ask Jonah Pike". The dashed note in the left menu gives the clicks.
The same result in dark mode.

Hard case, 1512 wide, signed in as Mei Arden, a commenter: only the bar's line says her changes go to each feature's approver (its (i) names Lena Vos and Avery Stone); the button still says "Change 4".
Phone 390: the report strip with the Ask button, above the list.
The same phone frame in dark mode.
